description.narrative:
The aftermath of the General Elections in Kenya on December 27th 2007 has been one of the most turbulent periods in post-independence Kenya. In particular the period just after the chaotic announcement of the winner of the election was one of intense violence in numerous parts of the country. Civilians have been beaten, homes burnt down, businesses destroyed and men, women and children killed. The Kenya Red Cross has reported that more than 500 people have been killed, and according to recent official figures released by the Government of Kenya (Jan 6th), there is officially an estimated 255,000 internally displaced people (IDPs) as a result of this violence.
A number of towns have been temporarily cut off and many major roads barricaded by various communities denying access to road users. This has affected the delivery of essential supplies to key markets and local communities. Among the most affected towns and cities are Kisumu, Eldoret, Nairobi, Nakuru, Kakamega, Busia, Kisumu, Mombasa, Kitale and Lugari. Most of the displaced groups have been camping at police stations, district administration camps, prison compounds, church compounds, local showgrounds and other public places where they feel some security and protection is available. People in these areas are homeless as they seek security in neighbouring districts and are in desperate need of shelter, food, water, medicine, personal hygiene items and clothing items particularly for children.
Alongside national government efforts to provide relief assistance, CAFOD is responding to this situation in the slums of Nairobi with food distributions, in Eldoret and Bungoma with food and non food items and in Kericho with non food items. CAFOD is also making efforts to reach some of the displaced groups in Mombasa at the Kenyan coast where it is estimated that over 3000 people have been displaced and 10 have so far died. This request to Jersey is for support to CAFOD’s response in Mombasa, in continued partnership with the Archdiocese of Mombasa, to reach 760 people (120 men, 217 females and 423 children) who have been camping in five Catholic Parishes compounds (Likoni, Cathedral, Bomu, Mikindani and Changamwe).
The Archdiocese of Mombasa has been providing direct assistance to these displaced people since they arrived in the parishes but are now running out of their existing resources. Shelter has been provided using existing parish facilities including meeting halls. They have also provided food such as maizemeal, rice, porridge and beans, as well as water from their existing supplies. Some additional food was provided by the Kenya Red Cross though supplies have run low. Each parish has sought to provide some basic medicines for minor ailments and refer individuals to local clinics where those services have been available. The parishes have, however, been unable to meet the growing needs of these groups and are in need of additional supplies of both food and non-food items. The Archdiocese has therefore requested support from CAFOD help reach out to these people.
